contexts.statement: OpenAI Math Audit #154: Pointwise multiple ergodic averages for mixing transformations.

Finite local catalog rows on a bounded dyadic interval with arbitrary Hilbert input and row-output spaces, persistent private columns, ordered support/observation refinements, and an ordinary joint Bessel bound. The task is independent verification or refutation of rows.tex lem:row-maximal and lem:row-depth; no full ergodic theorem is presumed.

definitions.catalog: Phi_v=(phi_v,gamma_v e_v), fixed private coordinate per label, dyadic birth J_v, D>=2, column norm<=D, abs(gamma_v)>=1/D, path birth count<=D
definitions.refinement: sigma_n refines pi_n and pi_(n+1) refines sigma_n; each row is supported on one whole pi_n cell and its tested adjoint has constant catalog coefficients on sigma_n cells
definitions.Bessel: sum_nu norm(A_nu z)^2 <= B^2 norm(z)^2 for every input z, before any test-dependent selection
definitions.depth_inputs: W deterministic consecutive blocks, max norm plus internal total variation <= W^(-1/2) a.e.; round reads are nondecreasing
definitions.source: Triple manuscript October-4-2026 build/paper/sections/rows.tex, lem:row-catalog, lem:row-maximal and lem:row-depth

contexts.statement: Finite-measure space with arbitrary finite measurable support and observation partitions in the original two refinement directions; local Hilbert-output rows with a joint all-input Bessel bound; one finite global persistent column family with uniform pointwise coefficient bounds m and M, 0<m<=M. Null support rows may be discarded. No dimension or schedule-length bound.

definitions.K(k,alpha): kappa^2/(2^k alpha^2)+(k+1)^2/(1-alpha)^2 for every integer k>=0 and real 0<alpha<1
definitions.block_radii: beta_b>=0 bounds the pointwise supremum plus internal total variation on each deterministic consecutive input block

claims.natural_statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 154 (Pointwise multiple ergodic averages for mixing transformations.; papers: Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations; Pointwise convergence of fourfold ergodic averages for mixing transformations; Triple ergodic averages with distinct integer slopes; Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations; Lean status: UNFORMALIZED (No Lean proof in openai/math)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Triple manuscript thm:main: on any probability space, for an invertible bimeasurable mixing probability-preserving T and every fixed bounded complex f1,f2,f3, averages at n,2n,3n converge a.e. along all positive lengths to the product of integrals; the null set may depend on the tuple.

Distinct-slopes manuscript thm:main: on any invertible bimeasurable mixing probability-preserving system, every fixed bounded triple at any fixed pairwise distinct nonzero integer slopes has a.e. all-length convergence to the product of integrals; both signs are permitted, and the null set may depend on slopes and functions.

Fourfold manuscript thm:main: on any probability space, for every invertible bimeasurable mixing probability-preserving T and every fixed bounded four-tuple, the averages at n,2n,3n,4n converge a.e. along all positive lengths to the product of integrals, without a mixing rate.

General manuscript thm:main: on an arbitrary probability space, every invertible bimeasurable mixing probability-preserving T, every integer n>=2, and every fixed bounded n-tuple have a.e. all-length convergence of consecutive-power averages to the product of integrals; no common exceptional set over tuples and no mixing rate are asserted.

Triple manuscript transfer.tex thm:depth-local: for any finite rooted dyadic tree, any summation subcollection and admissible local cancellative four-linear kernels, scalar depth inputs with their individual deterministic blockwise max-plus-variation normalizations have sum_I abs(I)*abs(H_I(f_0,s(I),...,f_3,s(I))) <= C_loc(c0,C0)*abs(J), uniformly in depths, blocks and finite data.

Distinct-slopes manuscript analytic input: the depth-dependent local estimate and smooth-profile oscillation/transference estimates extend to x+b_j t for every fixed four distinct integer slopes b0=0, with constants allowed to depend on those slopes; proof imports coefficient-independent results from H and V.

General inputs.tex thm:multiple-mixing and fourfold 02-structure.tex eq:all-orders-input: ordinary invertible mixing implies product limits of every fixed finite bounded tuple at integer times whose pairwise gaps tend to infinity. This is a substantial companion assertion, not verified here.

General inputs.tex lem:triple-convergence: on every standard invertible probability-preserving system, every fixed at-most-three bounded tuple at distinct positive integer slopes converges a.e. along all positive lengths. It relies on the distinct-slopes companion smooth oscillation and profile approximation without mixing.

The selected-law, tensor-packing, channel-preservation and saturated-extension arguments of fourfold Sections 3--6 yield its fourfold conclusion from higher-order mixing, lower-length pointwise convergence and the stated relative-structure inputs. This implication is an open audit obligation.

The minimal-correlation, selected-law, tensor-packing and square-array arguments in the general manuscript yield arbitrary consecutive length from the higher-mixing, triple pointwise and relative-structure inputs. This implication is an open audit obligation.

rows.tex lem:row-catalog: every available constant coefficient vector a satisfies D^(-1)||a||_2 <= ||sum_v a_v Phi_v(y)|| <= D^(3/2)||a||_2 a.e.; coefficients are unique and restrict unchanged to descendants, including after rebasing to a subroot.

rows.tex lem:row-maximal: under the original catalog, locality, ordered-refinement and Bessel hypotheses, every tested contiguous range has measure{M>lambda} <= min(abs(R),16(9+L_D^2)B^2 E_c/(9 lambda^2)) and ||M||_1 <= (8/3)sqrt(9+L_D^2)B sqrt(abs(R) E_c), L_D=1+ceil(5 log_2 D), for every lambda>0, uniformly in all finite dimensions, row counts and schedules.

rows.tex lem:row-depth: under every original maximal-row hypothesis and blockwise depth normalization, for every nondecreasing read schedule, (sum_n,nu ||A_nu F_s(n)||^2)^(1/2) <= (8/3)sqrt(9+L_D^2) B sqrt(abs(R)) <= (40/3)B log_2(2D)sqrt(abs(R)), uniformly in rows, depths and input blocks.

Universal combinatorial core: on arbitrary finite atom sets with support/observation equality refinements, any observation-local state update gives a support-local state at the next round and hence a single bucket for each whole row. For any finite row set, monotone pointwise bucket chronology and agreement of nonzero row values with their global owners imply exact partial-sum = completed-bucket-prefix + current-bucket-remainder identities. Disjoint global row masks preserve the summed subset Bessel energy budget.

The original universal lem:row-maximal and lem:row-depth follow without any companion analytic theorem, for every finite schedule and arbitrary Hilbert dimensions, by support-local whole-row buckets, the private-column frame bounds, binary-prefix energy, and blockwise Abel summation. A separate Lean theorem certifies only the explicitly stated combinatorial core, not the measure-theoretic theorem or the ergodic conclusions.

Triple manuscript transfer.tex thm:depth-local: for any finite rooted dyadic tree, any summation subcollection and admissible local cancellative four-linear kernels, scalar depth inputs with their individual deterministic blockwise max-plus-variation normalizations have sum_I abs(I)*abs(H_I(f_0,s(I),...,f_3,s(I))) <= C_loc(c0,C0)*abs(J), uniformly in depths, blocks and finite data.

claims.formal_statement:
import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

namespace CatalogRows

def evolve {X S : Type*} (update : ℕ → X → S → S) (initial : S) :
    ℕ → X → S
  | 0, _ => initial
  | n + 1, x => update n x (evolve update initial n x)

theorem state_support_local {X P O S : Type*}
    (support : ℕ → X → P) (observe : ℕ → X → O)
    (observation_refines : ∀ n x y,
      observe n x = observe n y → support n x = support n y)
    (next_support_refines : ∀ n x y,
      support (n + 1) x = support (n + 1) y → observe n x = observe n y)
    (update : ℕ → X → S → S) (initial : S)
    (update_local : ∀ n x y, observe n x = observe n y →
      ∀ s, update n x s = update n y s) :
    ∀ n x y, support n x = support n y →
      evolve update initial n x = evolve update initial n y := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
      intro x y _
      rfl
  | succ n ih =>
      intro x y h
      have ho := next_support_refines n x y h
      have hs := observation_refines n x y ho
      simp only [evolve]
      rw [ih x y hs]
      exact update_local n x y ho _

section Buckets

variable {V : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup V]

noncomputable def bucketStep (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (s : ℕ × V) (a : V) :
    ℕ × V :=
  if s.1 < T then
    if τ < ‖s.2 + a‖ then (s.1 + 1, 0) else (s.1, s.2 + a)
  else (s.1, 0)

theorem bucketStep_mono (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (s : ℕ × V) (a : V) :
    s.1 ≤ (bucketStep T τ s a).1 := by
  unfold bucketStep
  split_ifs <;> simp

theorem bucketStep_bound (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (s : ℕ × V) (a : V)
    (h : s.1 ≤ T) : (bucketStep T τ s a).1 ≤ T := by
  unfold bucketStep
  split_ifs <;> simp_all <;> omega

theorem bucketStep_residual (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (s : ℕ × V) (a : V)
    (hτ : 0 ≤ τ) : ‖(bucketStep T τ s a).2‖ ≤ τ := by
  unfold bucketStep
  split_ifs <;> simp_all

noncomputable def bucketState {X : Type*} (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ)
    (a : ℕ → X → V) : ℕ → X → ℕ × V :=
  evolve (fun n x s => bucketStep T τ s (a n x)) (0, 0)

theorem bucketState_mono {X : Type*} (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ)
    (a : ℕ → X → V) (x : X) :
    Monotone (fun n => (bucketState T τ a n x).1) := by
  apply monotone_nat_of_le_succ
  intro n
  exact bucketStep_mono T τ (bucketState T τ a n x) (a n x)

theorem bucketState_bound {X : Type*} (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ)
    (a : ℕ → X → V) (n : ℕ) (x : X) :
    (bucketState T τ a n x).1 ≤ T := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [bucketState, evolve]
  | succ n ih => exact bucketStep_bound T τ _ _ ih

theorem bucketState_residual {X : Type*} (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ)
    (a : ℕ → X → V) (hτ : 0 ≤ τ) (n : ℕ) (x : X) :
    ‖(bucketState T τ a n x).2‖ ≤ τ := by
  cases n with
  | zero => simpa [bucketState, evolve] using hτ
  | succ n => exact bucketStep_residual T τ _ _ hτ

theorem bucketState_support_local {X P O : Type*}
    (support : ℕ → X → P) (observe : ℕ → X → O)
    (observation_refines : ∀ n x y,
      observe n x = observe n y → support n x = support n y)
    (next_support_refines : ∀ n x y,
      support (n + 1) x = support (n + 1) y → observe n x = observe n y)
    (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (a : ℕ → X → V)
    (a_local : ∀ n x y, observe n x = observe n y → a n x = a n y) :
    ∀ n x y, support n x = support n y →
      bucketState T τ a n x = bucketState T τ a n y := by
  apply state_support_local support observe observation_refines next_support_refines
  intro n x y h s
  simp only [a_local n x y h]

theorem whole_row_bucket {X P O I : Type*}
    (support : ℕ → X → P) (observe : ℕ → X → O)
    (observation_refines : ∀ n x y,
      observe n x = observe n y → support n x = support n y)
    (next_support_refines : ∀ n x y,
      support (n + 1) x = support (n + 1) y → observe n x = observe n y)
    (T : ℕ) (τ : ℝ) (a : ℕ → X → V)
    (a_local : ∀ n x y, observe n x = observe n y → a n x = a n y)
    (round : I → ℕ) (representative : I → X) (r : I) (x : X)
    (hx : support (round r) x = support (round r) (representative r)) :
    (bucketState T τ a (round r) x).1 =
      (bucketState T τ a (round r) (representative r)).1 := by
  exact congrArg Prod.fst
    (bucketState_support_local support observe observation_refines
      next_support_refines T τ a a_local (round r) x (representative r) hx)

end Buckets

section Prefix

variable {I V : Type*} [AddCommMonoid V]

theorem completed_bucket_no_future
    (b : ℕ → ℕ) (hb : Monotone b) (time owner : I → ℕ) (f : I → V)
    (compatible : ∀ r, f r ≠ 0 → owner r = b (time r))
    (r : I) (j : ℕ) (hf : f r ≠ 0) (ho : owner r < b j) :
    time r < j := by
  by_contra ht
  have h := hb (Nat.le_of_not_gt ht)
  rw [← compatible r hf] at h
  omega

theorem completed_prefix_identity
    (rows : Finset I) (b : ℕ → ℕ) (hb : Monotone b)
    (time owner : I → ℕ) (f : I → V)
    (compatible : ∀ r ∈ rows, f r ≠ 0 → owner r = b (time r))
    (j : ℕ) :
    (∑ r ∈ rows, if time r < j then f r else 0) =
      (∑ r ∈ rows, if owner r < b j then f r else 0) +
      ∑ r ∈ rows, if time r < j ∧ owner r = b j then f r else 0 := by
  classical
  rw [← Finset.sum_add_distrib]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro r hr
  by_cases hf : f r = 0
  · simp [hf]
  have ho := compatible r hr hf
  by_cases ht : time r < j
  · have hle : owner r ≤ b j := by
      rw [ho]
      exact hb (Nat.le_of_lt ht)
    by_cases hk : owner r < b j
    · have hne : owner r ≠ b j := ne_of_lt hk
      simp [ht, hk, hne]
    · have he : owner r = b j := by omega
      simp [ht, hk, he]
  · have hk : ¬owner r < b j := by
      have h := hb (Nat.le_of_not_gt ht)
      rw [← ho] at h
      omega
    simp [ht, hk]

end Prefix

section Energy

variable {I K V : Type*} [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    [NormedAddCommGroup V]

theorem disjoint_mask_energy
    (rows : Finset I) (owner : I → Option K) (f : I → V) (w : I → ℝ)
    (hw : ∀ r ∈ rows, 0 ≤ w r)
    (subset_bessel : ∀ s : Finset I, s ⊆ rows →
      ‖∑ r ∈ s, f r‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∑ r ∈ s, w r) :
    (∑ k : K, ‖∑ r ∈ rows.filter (fun r => owner r = some k), f r‖ ^ 2) ≤
      ∑ r ∈ rows, w r := by
  classical
  calc
    (∑ k : K, ‖∑ r ∈ rows.filter (fun r => owner r = some k), f r‖ ^ 2)
        ≤ ∑ k : K, ∑ r ∈ rows.filter (fun r => owner r = some k), w r := by
          apply Finset.sum_le_sum
          intro k _
          exact subset_bessel _ (Finset.filter_subset _ _)
    _ = ∑ r ∈ rows, ∑ k : K, if owner r = some k then w r else 0 := by
          simp_rw [Finset.sum_filter]
          rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    _ ≤ ∑ r ∈ rows, w r := by
          apply Finset.sum_le_sum
          intro r hr
          cases ho : owner r with
          | none => simpa [ho] using hw r hr
          | some k => simp [ho]

end Energy

theorem improved_constant (L : ℝ) (hL : 6 ≤ L) :
    81 + (324 / 49 : ℝ) * L ^ 2 <
      (64 / 9 : ℝ) * (9 + L ^ 2) := by
  have hsq : 36 ≤ L ^ 2 := by nlinarith
  nlinarith

end CatalogRows

#print axioms CatalogRows.state_support_local
#print axioms CatalogRows.whole_row_bucket
#print axioms CatalogRows.completed_prefix_identity
#print axioms CatalogRows.disjoint_mask_energy
#print axioms CatalogRows.improved_constant

claims.natural_statement: For all data in this context, all arbitrary tests on every contiguous range, every k>=0, 0<alpha<1 and lambda>0, the prefix maximum M satisfies mu{M>lambda}<=min(mu(X),K(k,alpha) B^2 E/lambda^2) and ||M||_1<=2 sqrt(K(k,alpha)) B sqrt(mu(X) E), with E the total squared test norm. The statement covers every finite schedule and arbitrary Hilbert dimensions.

For all data in this context and all strongly measurable input schedules with block radii beta_b and nondecreasing repeated reads, the depth output norm is <=2 sqrt(K(k,alpha)) B sqrt(mu(X)) sqrt(sum_b beta_b^2) for every k>=0 and 0<alpha<1, with no row-count, schedule-length, block-count or dimension dependence.

Under every original hypothesis of rows.tex lem:row-maximal and lem:row-depth, both maximal bounds and the depth bound hold with Cprime_D=sqrt(81+(324/49)L_D^2), L_D=1+ceil(5 log_2 D), replacing C_D. Cprime_D<C_D for every D>=2. In particular at D=2 the squared constant improves from 320 to 15633/49. No optimality or novelty claim is made.
